trainingmodels

trainingmodels provides mathematical models of training load and training response used in sport science. The package is experimental: its interface may still change.

Version 0.0.3 contains:

  • as_daily_load(): builds a complete daily calendar of training load from session data, for one or several athletes;
  • srpe_load(): session RPE load (RPE x duration; Foster 1998, Foster et al. 2001);
  • rolling_load(): rolling sum and mean of the daily load over a window;
  • monotony_strain(): Foster’s training monotony and strain over a rolling window;
  • simulate_banister(): simulation of the Banister impulse-response model (two-component or fitness-only) from parameters given by the user;
  • session_response() and constant_training(): response to a single session and to constant daily training;
  • half_life() and time_constant(): conversion between time constants and half-lives.

The Banister model is simulated, not fitted: estimating its parameters from data is planned for version 0.1.0. Acute:chronic workload ratios and EWMA-based loads are in the ACWR package, not here.

Example

The week of Foster (1998, Table 1):

library(trainingmodels)
load <- srpe_load(c(5, 7, 2, 6, 7, 2, 7), c(180, 120, 20, 90, 75, 20, 120))
week <- data.frame(date = as.Date("2026-01-04") + 0:6, load = load)
x <- as_daily_load(week, date = "date", load = "load")
monotony_strain(x)

On the seventh day the weekly load is 3725, the monotony 1.45 and the strain 5397.

The example of Morton et al. (1990): load 100 every day for 60 days, then rest.

x <- as_daily_load(
  data.frame(date = as.Date("2026-01-01") + 0:119,
             load = c(rep(100, 60), rep(0, 60))),
  date = "date", load = "load"
)
sim <- simulate_banister(x, k1 = 1, tau1 = 45, k2 = 2, tau2 = 15,
                         same_day_load = "include")
which.min(sim$predicted)
session_response(k1 = 1, tau1 = 45, k2 = 2, tau2 = 15)

Predicted performance is lowest on day 16; one session lowers performance for about 16 days and raises it most after about 40 days.

Design decisions are recorded in DECISIONS.md, formulas and their verification in MODELS.md, and the use of AI assistance is disclosed in AI_USAGE.md.

Installation

The development version can be installed with:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("JorgeDelro/trainingmodels")
